nodes.label: Recovering Clinical Utility Under Differential Privacy (Base Paper)
Yeom et al. Loss-Threshold Membership-Inference Attack
Fixed-0.5-Threshold / Label-Shift Artifact
nodes.rationale: Client 1's apparent FedAvg collapse (78.9% local -> 34.7% FedAvg) was diagnosed as substantially a fixed 0.5 decision-threshold artifact under per-client label shift, not a training failure: AUC stayed 0.822 and balanced accuracy was 0.500 (chance) for every one of the 5 clients under the unweighted, fixed-threshold setup. This motivated per-client pos_weight loss weighting and per-client threshold tuning as the fix.

nodes.label: Federated Pooling as Dominant Privacy Mechanism
nodes.rationale: MIA audit found fully-local per-hospital models leak measurably more (attack AUC up to 0.63) than the shared FedAvg/FedProx model (attack AUC ~0.485, indistinguishable from 0.5) at every epsilon including no DP -- suggesting pooling itself, not DP noise, is the dominant privacy mechanism in this setup. Flagged as provisional: these models predate the fixed-threshold correction and should be re-run.

nodes.label: CDC Diabetes Health Indicators Dataset (UCI id 891)
No-BatchNorm Model Design Decision
nodes.rationale: Opacus's per-sample gradient computation for DP-SGD does not support BatchNorm, so DiabetesMLP was designed with LayerNorm instead of BatchNorm from Step 4 onward (before any FL/DP code existed) specifically to avoid a rework later. Verified via opacus.validators.ModuleValidator.validate().

nodes.label: Flower start_simulation Over ServerApp/flwr run
nodes.rationale: Flower's simulation mode (virtual clients in one process) was chosen over literal Docker-per-hospital or the newer ServerApp/flower-superlink deployment model because it is standard practice in published FL research and avoids networking/ops complexity for a free-tier-compute, PyTorch-still-learning team. This is a legitimate simplification, not a corner cut -- Docker is mentioned only as a future-deployment discussion paragraph.

nodes.label: External Review Finding: FedProx Is Not Personalization
nodes.rationale: An outside pre-submission review found that FedProx produces one shared global model (Li et al. 2020), so the project's title/research question claiming 'personalized FL' is not supported by what is implemented. Response plan: either reframe (drop the claim) or implement real personalization (Ditto/FedPer).

nodes.label: Temporal Denoising of DP Noise via Server-Side Momentum
nodes.rationale: Because DP noise is zero-mean Gaussian and independent across rounds, FedCVR's exponential moving averages (Adam-style first/second moment estimates) progressively cancel the noise while accumulating the true gradient signal -- the theoretical basis for FedCVR recovering utility under DP.

nodes.label: Extreme Class Imbalance Destabilizing Precision Metrics
nodes.rationale: The Switzerland cohort (~94% positive prevalence after outcome binarization) offers very few negative cases in its held-out partition, making precision-sensitive metrics unstable for that fold -- flagged as a limitation/threat to validity.
